title: Module 5: Healthcare Team, Escalation & Conflict Resolution

questions.stem: What is professionalism in this context?
options: Looking professional and being polite only
Wearing a name tag and arriving on time
Agreeing with colleagues at all times
What patients and colleagues can consistently expect from us — reflected in the decisions we make when no one is standing beside us
questions.explanation: Professionalism appears in consistent expectations and everyday decisions, not just appearance or manners.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: What is accountability?
options: Blaming others when things go wrong
Being answerable for the work we accept and for what we do with the information available to us
questions.explanation: Accountability means owning the work and the information — it does not mean a competent professional never makes a mistake.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: Which statement about mistakes and accountability is correct?
options: Mistakes should be hidden to protect the team
We all make mistakes — accountability means being able to own them and act on them
Mistakes are only the employer's concern
questions.explanation: Owning mistakes honestly is the essence of accountability.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: Which statement about confidence is correct?
options: Confidence alone is not enough — education, demonstrated competence, workplace policy, and authority under which you act must also be considered
questions.explanation: Confidence must be supported by education, demonstrated competence, policy, and authority.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: Which statement about learning in this profession is TRUE?
options: Learning is only needed after a complaint
Experience removes the need for learning
Graduation is the beginning of continued competence, not the end of learning
questions.explanation: Equipment, evidence, and scope all change, so learning continues throughout a career.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: Which set best matches what a cardiac sonographer is accountable for?
options: Assigned duties, image acquisition and measurements, following policies and protocols while using judgement, recognizing personal limitations, and reporting concerns appropriately
questions.explanation: These five areas define the sonographer's accountability in the cardiac setting.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: A protocol calls for several remaining views, but the patient is becoming unstable. What does the protocol rule require?
options: Finish the protocol before checking on the patient
The protocol always overrides patient condition
A protocol guides a routine echo, but it does not require ignoring a patient who is becoming unstable simply because images remain
questions.explanation: Patient condition governs — continuing an unstable patient through a protocol is unsafe practice.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: Which statement about protocol and judgement is correct?
options: Apply protocols rigidly regardless of condition
Follow protocols while using professional judgement for the patient's actual condition
questions.explanation: Accountability includes following protocols and using judgement together.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: A sonographer recognizes a limitation in their own skills during a study. What does accountability require?
options: Recognize the limitation and report concerns appropriately, seeking help through the approved pathway
Continue regardless and hope for the best
Hide the limitation from the team
questions.explanation: Recognizing personal limitations and reporting concerns are explicit accountability duties.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: What does "a safe sonographer does not try to become every member of the healthcare team" mean?
options: Safe care comes from understanding your own role, recognizing when another person's expertise is needed, and ensuring information reaches the right person
Sonographers should learn every other role completely
questions.explanation: Role clarity — not role expansion — is what makes care safe.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: Which statement about safe care is TRUE?
options: Safe care requires answering every question alone
Safe care does not depend on knowing everything
Safe care is the physician's responsibility alone
questions.explanation: Recognizing what you do not know and connecting to the right person is safe practice.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: What does the sonographer's role include when entering the examination room?
options: Acquiring and optimizing echo information, recognizing and reporting limitations, and communicating concerns through the approved pathway
questions.explanation: The role is acquisition, optimization, limitation reporting, and communication — not independent diagnosis or treatment.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: The sonographer should NOT enter the room having:
options: Already decided what is wrong with the patient
questions.explanation: Entering with a pre-made diagnosis biases the examination and exceeds the role.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: Which statement about respect in the workplace is correct?
options: Respect includes how we speak to patients, how we speak about them when they are absent, and how we treat colleagues during stressful moments
questions.explanation: Respectful conduct extends to absent patients and colleagues under pressure.
tags: Professionalism and Accountability

questions.stem: How is successful communication defined?
options: When the sender and receiver understand the message in the same way
When the message is sent quickly
When the sender talks the most
questions.explanation: The practical test is whether the other person received the message we intended.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: What is the closed loop of communication?
options: Send → receive → confirm, with the receiver reporting back when the call is completed or if they cannot reach someone
questions.explanation: Confirmation and report-back close the loop; the task is verified as accepted and acted upon.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement about silence is correct?
options: Silence does not prove that an action happened
questions.explanation: Without confirmation, you cannot know whether the action occurred.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: You ask a colleague to call cardiology about an urgent concern. What best completes the communication loop?
options: The colleague confirms the action and reports back
You mention it once and leave
questions.explanation: Closed-loop communication confirms the task was accepted and the message reached the intended person.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement about professional communication is correct?
options: Professional communication is what you say, how you say it, what you document, what you confirm, and what you escalate
Professional communication is speaking politely only
Professional communication applies only to patients
questions.explanation: The definition encompasses speech, manner, documentation, confirmation, and escalation.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement about sending and receiving information is TRUE?
options: Both sending and receiving are responsibilities — checking the message was understood belongs to the process
questions.explanation: Professional communication includes sending, receiving, checking understanding, and responding appropriately.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which channel is safe for communicating an urgent patient concern?
options: The approved communication pathway for the organization
A note left where no one confirms receipt
questions.explanation: Hallway conversations, personal texts, and unconfirmed notes are not safe communication.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement about busy departments and communication is correct?
options: Busy departments do not need closed loops
Interruptions and misunderstandings are common, so confirmation is essential
questions.explanation: In busy settings, people get interrupted, misunderstand, or assume someone else is handling it — hence confirmation.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: What should a sonographer do after requesting an action from a colleague?
options: Confirm the colleague accepted the task and follow up on the report-back
questions.explanation: Acceptance and report-back are what close the loop.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which example best demonstrates closed-loop communication?
options: "Please call Cardiology now and tell them Jordan is more short of breath" → "I'm calling Cardiology now" → the colleague reports back that the call was made
A note is left on the desk
The concern is mentioned in the hallway
The request is sent by personal text
questions.explanation: The exchange shows send, receive-confirmation, and report-back — a complete loop.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement about communication and patient safety is TRUE?
options: Communication is part of safe care, not an optional courtesy
questions.explanation: Information reaching the right person in time is a component of care itself.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: What is the danger of assuming "someone else is handling it"?
options: The task may fall through entirely, leaving the patient without needed action
questions.explanation: Assumption is a common cause of uncompleted tasks and missed care.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement about urgent or stat communication is correct?
options: Urgency reduces the need for confirmation
The closed loop matters most when the concern is urgent or stat
Urgent messages can wait for the routine report
questions.explanation: The higher the stakes, the more important confirmation becomes.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: A colleague confirms they will call the cardiologist but never reports back. What should you do?
options: Assume it is done because they said they would
Follow up to confirm the action was completed, continuing through the approved pathway as needed
Blame the colleague if it fails
questions.explanation: Verbal acceptance without report-back leaves the loop open; follow-up closes it.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which pair of actions best represents the full communication responsibility?
options: Send the message clearly, and confirm it was received and acted upon
questions.explanation: Clear sending plus confirmation of receipt and action completes the responsibility.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement summarizes the relationship between communication and imaging?
options: Technical skill creates the images; communication makes the images useful
Communication is secondary to image quality
questions.explanation: The right observation must reach the right person with clarity and urgency to matter.
tags: Communication Fundamentals and the Closed Loop

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the sonographer's communication in practice?
options: Use technical terms to sound expert
Identify yourself and the patient, explain what is happening, speak in plain language, check understanding, document accurately, communicate concerns promptly, and escalate when the condition changes
Document only at the end of the day
questions.explanation: These actions together make up everyday professional communication in the examination room.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which introduction is most appropriate?
options: "Lie down and take your shirt off."
"Hi, Jordan. My name is Jillian. I'm the echo tech today completing your echocardiogram."
questions.explanation: The introduction names the practitioner, identifies the patient, and states the purpose.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: What is teach-back?
options: Asking the patient to explain back, in their own words, what they understand will happen — a check on the explanation, not a test of the patient
questions.explanation: Teach-back verifies that the explanation was clear, without implying the patient is being examined.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which phrasing best demonstrates teach-back?
options: "Just so I know I explained it clearly, can you tell me how we are going to position you?"
"You know what an echo is, right?"
questions.explanation: The phrasing puts the check on the explanation rather than on the patient.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which elements make up non-verbal communication?
options: Eye contact, facial expression, posture, tone of voice, and professional presence
questions.explanation: Non-verbal signals shape how messages are received.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: A sonographer says "take your time" while looking at the clock and tapping a foot. What is the problem?
options: The actions contradict the words — the patient receives the opposite message
questions.explanation: Actions can contradict words; consistency between verbal and non-verbal messages matters.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: What does limited eye contact by a patient or practitioner automatically mean?
options: Nothing automatic — limited eye contact does not automatically mean dishonesty or disengagement
questions.explanation: Cultural norms, anxiety, and many other factors influence eye contact; no single meaning should be assumed.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: What should happen before touching or repositioning a patient?
options: Explain what you are doing and why
questions.explanation: Explaining before touching respects the patient and supports ongoing consent.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which statement about jargon is correct?
options: Avoid unexplained jargon; use everyday words one step at a time
questions.explanation: Plain language supports understanding; jargon without explanation creates barriers.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which statement should be avoided when speaking with a patient?
options: An explanation of what will happen next
A promise you cannot keep — such as a guaranteed result or a guaranteed timeframe
An honest description of the examination
questions.explanation: Promises that cannot be supported damage trust and may be untrue.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which comment about another staff member should never be made to a patient?
options: The name of the interpreting physician
The name of the nurse involved
The role of the care team
Any negative or critical comment about colleagues
questions.explanation: Speaking poorly about colleagues undermines confidence in the care team.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: How should exposure and positioning be handled for female patients?
options: Explain the required exposure and positioning, use appropriate draping, and check comfort throughout the scan
questions.explanation: Explanation, draping, and ongoing comfort checks protect dignity during a sensitive examination.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Why should comfort be checked throughout the examination rather than only at the start?
options: It is only required for anxious patients
Comfort and willingness can change during the examination, and consent is ongoing
questions.explanation: A single initial check cannot capture a changing situation — ongoing checks respect autonomy.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which statement about documentation as communication is correct?
options: Documentation is a form of communication — accurate entries tell the next clinician what happened
Documentation matters only in legal proceedings
questions.explanation: The clinical record communicates facts to everyone who relies on them afterward.
tags: Professional Communication Skills with Patients

questions.stem: Which list correctly matches common communication barriers?
options: Equipment brand, software version, and settings
Language, hearing, health literacy, anxiety, pain, cultural or personal comfort, and background noise
questions.explanation: These are the barriers taught as common obstacles to understanding in the examination room.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: What does a communication barrier usually mean?
options: It usually means our usual approach is not working — not that the patient is difficult
questions.explanation: A barrier is a signal to adapt the approach, not a judgement about the patient.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: Which set best matches the taught barrier solutions?
options: Repeating loudly, rushing, guessing, and ignoring
Written orders only, silence, avoidance, and hurry
Family translation, jargon, pressure, and repetition
Plain language, slowing down, a qualified interpreter, and teach-back
questions.explanation: These four strategies adapt the communication to the barrier.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: A patient does not understand English. What does repeating the same sentence more loudly accomplish?
options: It proves the patient is difficult
Nothing useful — repeating the same sentence more loudly will not solve a language difference
questions.explanation: Volume does not bridge a language gap; a qualified interpreter does.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: When is a qualified interpreter the appropriate solution?
options: Only when the patient requests one in writing
Never — family members are always used
When a language difference exists and a qualified interpreter is available and appropriate
questions.explanation: Interpreter use is a standard response to language barriers and a common interview topic.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: When using an interpreter, whom should you speak to?
options: The patient, not the interpreter — using short clear sentences and pausing
questions.explanation: Speaking to the patient maintains the therapeutic relationship and reduces filtering.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: Why are family members not always appropriate as interpreters?
options: They may filter information, misunderstand terminology, or create privacy concerns
questions.explanation: Filtering, misunderstanding, and privacy risks make qualified interpreters preferable.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: Which language habits best support interpreter-assisted communication?
options: Long complex sentences with medical terms
Short clear sentences, pauses, and avoiding slang, unexplained abbreviations, and long technical explanations
questions.explanation: Chunked, plain speech is interpretable; dense jargon is not.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: A long technical explanation is making an anxious patient more anxious. What should you do?
options: Shorten and simplify the explanation — a long technical explanation can make anxiety worse
questions.explanation: Concise plain-language explanation reduces anxiety better than technical density.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: When working with a patient who is hard of hearing, what is the FIRST step?
options: Ask what support works best for them — one approach does not suit every patient
questions.explanation: Individual needs differ; asking identifies the most effective support.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: Which set best matches hearing-supportive communication?
options: Shout, turn away, and speak over background noise
Gain attention before speaking, face the person directly with your mouth visible, reduce background noise, and speak clearly at a natural pace
Whisper, leave the room, and speak quickly
questions.explanation: These techniques maximize the patient's ability to hear and lip-read.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: Why should you not shout at a patient who is hard of hearing?
options: Shouting is always forbidden by policy only
Shouting distorts speech and may feel disrespectful — it reduces rather than improves understanding
questions.explanation: Distortion from shouting makes lip-reading and comprehension harder.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: Which supports may help a patient with hearing loss?
options: Hearing devices, written instructions, captioning, and interpreters
questions.explanation: Multiple modalities — devices, writing, captioning, interpreters — can bridge hearing barriers.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: What is cultural safety in communication?
options: Assuming all patients share your background
Avoiding all patients from other cultures
It begins when we recognize our own way of communicating is not automatically universal
questions.explanation: Cultural safety starts with self-awareness; memorizing cultural rules can create stereotypes, so respectful questions are preferred.
tags: Communication Barriers, Language, Culture and Hearing

questions.stem: What does people-centred care mean?
options: Scanning technique is the only priority
We are scanning a person, not simply acquiring pictures of the heart
questions.explanation: People-centred care attends to the person behind the images — though it does not mean promising every request.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: What is empathy in this context?
options: Solving every problem the patient raises
Noticing the emotion and responding without dismissing it — it does not require fixing every feeling
Agreeing with everything the patient says
questions.explanation: Empathy acknowledges emotion and responds appropriately, without taking on roles outside the scope.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: Which statement about empathy's boundaries is correct?
options: Avoid excessive personal details, do not become the patient's counsellor, and make no decisions outside your role
Empathy requires becoming the patient's friend
questions.explanation: Empathy is bounded by the professional role.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: A patient says, "I'm scared something's wrong." Which response best reflects empathy?
options: "I can see that you're worried. I will explain what I'm doing throughout, and I'll make sure the appropriate physician receives the study and if there are any concerns."
questions.explanation: The response notices the emotion, promises clear communication, and ensures the physician receives the study.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: A patient arrives upset about a previous experience. What is an appropriate response before beginning?
options: "That sounds difficult. Before we begin, is there anything that would help you feel more comfortable during the echo?"
questions.explanation: The response acknowledges the experience and asks a respectful, practical question.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: What is the problem with saying "I know exactly how you feel"?
options: It assumes an experience you cannot fully know — it dismisses rather than acknowledges the patient's individual feeling
questions.explanation: Presuming to share the patient's exact feeling can invalidate their individual experience.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: What is the problem with saying "At least it is not..." to a patient?
options: It minimizes the patient's concern rather than acknowledging it
questions.explanation: Comparisons that minimize a concern dismiss the emotion instead of responding to it.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: What is the problem with "There's nothing to worry about"?
options: We do not actually know that, and it gives unauthorized reassurance that may be wrong
questions.explanation: False reassurance can damage trust, exceed the role, and be incorrect.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: What is the problem with "Just try to relax"?
options: It is dismissive and gives an instruction without addressing the cause of the anxiety
questions.explanation: The instruction dismisses the emotion instead of exploring and responding to it.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: Which statement about false reassurance is correct?
options: It is appropriate for anxious patients
It may feel kind in the moment, but it can damage trust, may give information we are not authorized to provide, and it can also be wrong
It reduces the need for physician review
It is authorized when the scan looks normal
questions.explanation: These three risks make false reassurance inappropriate despite good intentions.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: A patient asks, "Did you find anything serious?" Which three elements are required in the response?
options: Acknowledge the concern, explain the review process, and ensure the patient knows the concern will reach the appropriate clinician
questions.explanation: These three elements answer the question honestly within the professional role.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: A patient's concern is raised during an inpatient echo. Who else should be informed?
options: No one until the report is complete
questions.explanation: For inpatients, the nurse should also know about the concern.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: Why is the response "I can't tell you anything" inadequate?
options: It is abrupt and unhelpful — the concern should be redirected helpfully to the proper process and person
questions.explanation: Honest role limits should be paired with a helpful redirect, not a refusal.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: A patient is labelled "uncooperative" in conversation. What might that label be missing?
options: Nothing — the label is usually complete
Fear, pain, a communication need, or a previous harmful experience — such as being pushed hard and bruised by a previous technician
questions.explanation: Behaviour often reflects unmet needs; asking why is more informative than labeling.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: A frustrated patient swears during the examination. What is the most professional response?
options: Recognize that frustration often reflects fear, pain, or previous experience; do not match the emotion or become defensive; set respectful limits if behaviour becomes unsafe
questions.explanation: Understanding the likely cause, staying calm, and setting respectful limits keeps the encounter safe.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: Which statement about people-centred communication is TRUE?
options: It respects the person's emotions, choices, and dignity while staying within the professional role
It requires agreeing with every request
It applies only to anxious patients
questions.explanation: People-centred communication balances respect for the person with professional boundaries.
tags: Empathy, People-Centred Care and Responses to Avoid

questions.stem: Which set best matches the information the team needs from the sonographer?
options: The patient's entire medical history and social details
Patient history affecting the echo, study quality and limitations, objective observations requiring review, and any change in the patient's condition
questions.explanation: These four categories are what the team actually needs to act on.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: Why is "more information" not always better?
options: Information overload is a legal violation
Unrelated detail hides the important point
questions.explanation: Relevant information communicates clearly; extraneous detail obscures the key point.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: What does accuracy in team communication require?
options: Distinguishing the patient's report, your direct observation, and the conclusion that belongs to the interpreting physician
questions.explanation: These three sources must be clearly separated so the receiver can weigh them correctly.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: What does timeliness mean for clinical communication?
options: Communicating urgent information while it can still affect care, not documenting it at the end of the day
Waiting for the report to be finalized
questions.explanation: Details fade and care windows close — urgent information must move immediately.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a safe communication channel for a clinical concern?
options: A direct phone call with confirmation
questions.explanation: Personal texts, hallway conversations, and unconfirmed notes are not safe channels.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: Which set correctly lists the forms of professional communication?
questions.explanation: These four forms carry clinical information through the system.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: What is the documentation test for communication?
options: "Could another qualified person understand what happened, what I observed, and what action I took?"
"Would this impress a court more than a colleague?"
questions.explanation: If another qualified person cannot reconstruct the event, the record may not support continuity of care.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: Which handoff statement is most useful?
options: "Jordan became more short of breath while lying flat, and I stopped the echo to sit him upright."
questions.explanation: The specific statement gives the receiver something clear enough to act on.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: What does an effective escalation require?
options: Reaching someone who can act and confirming the message was received and understood
Adding a note to the chart only
questions.explanation: Escalation is complete only when an actionable person has received and confirmed the message.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: What should a consultation communication identify?
options: Who is being asked to review the concern, why it is being raised, what has already been attempted, and what requires attention
questions.explanation: These elements let the consultant act efficiently on the concern.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: A patient with a technical limitation will be transferred to CT after the echo. Why does the limitation matter?
options: It does not matter outside the echo lab
Only the sonographer needs to know
It should be erased before transfer
The limitation needs to follow the study so the next person — such as the CT technologist — knows what was and was not obtained
questions.explanation: Limitations must travel with the study so subsequent testing is informed.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: Which combination BEST matches the four qualities of information passed beyond the encounter?
options: Relevant — history and limitations; Objective — reports, observations, and physician conclusions distinguished; Timely — while it can still affect care; Verified — confirmed received and understood
Verbal only, opinionated, postponed, and assumed
questions.explanation: These four qualities — relevant, objective, timely, verified — define useful team information.
tags: Communication Beyond the Encounter: Relevant, Objective, Timely, Verified

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly matches the cardiac care pathway?
options: Echocardiogram → symptoms → laboratory testing → discharge → nothing
Symptom and urgent assessment → ECG and laboratory testing → echocardiogram → treatment planning or further investigation → monitoring and follow-up
Imaging only; the other steps are unnecessary
questions.explanation: The pathway moves from assessment through testing, imaging, planning, and follow-up.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What does each step of the pathway depend on?
options: Information reaching the right person at the right time
questions.explanation: Each step remains incomplete unless the next person receives the right information in time.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: Which is a common point where information is lost in the pathway?
options: The order does not include the real clinical question
questions.explanation: An order lacking the clinical question leaves the examination less focused and useful.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: A patient's symptoms change during transport to the echo lab, but nobody tells the team. Where has communication failed?
options: Nowhere — transport is not a communication point
At the transport step — the change in condition must be communicated to the receiving team
questions.explanation: Transport is a handoff point where changing conditions must travel with the patient.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: An urgent observation is documented in the record but never escalated. What is the result?
options: The report will automatically alert someone
The patient will inform the team
The observation may never reach someone who can act in time — documentation alone is not escalation
questions.explanation: Recording an urgent observation without escalating it can delay care.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What should a sonographer do BEFORE scanning?
options: Skip the order review when busy
Verify the request and gather the relevant history
questions.explanation: Pre-scan verification of the request and history sets up a focused, safe examination.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What is the sonographer's communication responsibility DURING the examination?
options: Monitor the patient's tolerance and condition
Complete the study regardless of condition
questions.explanation: Monitoring tolerance and condition during scanning allows timely adaptation and escalation.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What are the sonographer's responsibilities AFTER the examination?
options: Leave immediately after the last image
Wait for someone else to notice concerns
Save and label the study, document limitations, and communicate concerns through the approved pathway
questions.explanation: Post-study tasks ensure the images are usable and concerns are transmitted.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What is the cardiologist's role on the team?
options: Integrating clinical and diagnostic information and directing medical management
questions.explanation: The cardiologist integrates information and directs medical management.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What is the registered nurse's role in the cardiac team?
options: Ongoing assessment, medication administration, and coordination and communication between tests
questions.explanation: The nurse's ongoing assessment often detects changes between diagnostic encounters.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What is the respiratory therapist's role?
questions.explanation: Respiratory therapists address breathing, oxygenation, and ventilation.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What does a cardiac diagnostic technologist (CBT) do?
options: ECG, ambulatory monitoring, and stress testing
questions.explanation: CBT technologists perform ECG, ambulatory monitoring, and stress testing.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What is the cardiac sonographer's distinctive contribution?
options: Acquiring and optimizing echo information about cardiac structure and function, with measurements, technical observations, and communication of concerns
questions.explanation: The sonographer's contribution is imaging, measurement, observation, and communication — not diagnosis or treatment.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: Which of the following is an allied health role in cardiac care?
options: Pharmacist, physiotherapist, interpreter, dietitian, and discharge planner
questions.explanation: These allied health roles contribute medications, mobility, communication, nutrition, and discharge planning.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: Which is a support role that affects echo workflow?
options: Porters and transport, who communicate mobility and oxygen needs and changes
questions.explanation: Transport staff communicate mobility and oxygen needs — information that matters directly to the examination.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What is the risk when an urgent study does not transfer to PACS?
options: No risk — the images remain on the machine
It is a technical problem that can become a clinical delay — the images must reach the interpreting team
questions.explanation: Images that never reach PACS cannot be interpreted in time to affect care.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: What is the purpose of listing the cardiac team roles?
options: To rank the professions by importance
To reduce the number of team members
To clarify who holds the knowledge and authority for each need — not to create a ranking
questions.explanation: The role list clarifies knowledge and authority; it is explicitly not a ranking.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: Which question best captures the spirit of the team-role framework?
options: Who can I blame if this fails?
Who has the right knowledge and authority for this need, and how do I connect them with the patient?
questions.explanation: Connecting the need to the right person — not ranking roles — is the framework's purpose.
tags: The Cardiac Care Pathway and Team Roles

questions.stem: Which two assumptions does role clarity protect against?
options: "The patient is difficult" and "The order is wrong"
"Someone else may have done it" and "I thought I was allowed to do it"
"The report is late" and "The file is lost"
questions.explanation: Clear roles prevent both dropped tasks and unauthorized actions.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: When responsibilities vary between workplaces, what is the correct approach?
options: Assume your previous workplace's rules apply
When you are uncertain, clarify before acting on it
Wait for a mistake to clarify roles
questions.explanation: Variation between workplaces makes clarification the safe response to uncertainty.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: A patient becomes acutely more short of breath during the scan. What is the correct first response?
options: Obtain immediate clinical help through the approved escalation pathway — stay with the patient and assess within your role
Send an email to the cardiologist
Wait for the final report to flag it
questions.explanation: Immediate clinical help through the approved pathway is required — not email, protocol completion, or waiting.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: A study will not transfer to PACS. What should the sonographer do?
options: Ignore the failure — the images remain on the machine
Contact imaging informatics or PACS support per the local process, protect the study, verify patient information, and communicate any clinical urgency
questions.explanation: A technical failure does not remove the need for the images to reach the interpreting team.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: A patient asks which medication will be started after their echo. What is the correct response?
options: Acknowledge the question and connect the patient to an authorized prescriber or care-team member, such as the physician or pharmacist
Guess based on what you think the diagnosis is
Read the chart and prescribe verbally
questions.explanation: Treatment information belongs to authorized prescribers or care-team members; the sonographer connects the patient.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: An ultrasound probe is damaged and peeling. What should the sonographer do?
options: Continue because the schedule is busy
Use it only on routine patients
Stop using the equipment, protect the patient, and follow the biomedical or workplace reporting process
questions.explanation: Continued use can harm the patient and degrade images; the equipment must be reported and removed from use.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: Why should unsafe equipment never be continued with "because we are busy"?
options: It can harm the patient, and the images themselves will not be good
questions.explanation: Patient safety and image quality both suffer from unsafe equipment.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: Which statement about role clarity is TRUE?
options: Role clarity is only for managers
A task that everyone assumes belongs to someone else is not collaboration
questions.explanation: Assumed diffusion of responsibility causes tasks to be dropped; clarity assigns action.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: What does "the right first contact" depend on?
options: The need — who has the knowledge and authority for it
questions.explanation: Matching the need to the person with knowledge and authority gets help fastest.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: Which combination BEST represents effective role clarity in practice?
options: Perform every role yourself, assume others will act, and avoid questions
Know your own role, recognize when another expertise is needed, clarify uncertain responsibilities, and connect the patient to the person with the right knowledge and authority
Rank roles, assign blame, and avoid escalation
Wait for others to define your role for you
questions.explanation: Role clarity combines self-knowledge, recognition of others' expertise, clarification, and connection.
tags: Role Clarity and First Contact

questions.stem: Which set best matches the cardiac sonographer's scope in practice?
options: Selecting views, adjusting settings, adapting the echo to the clinical question and the patient's condition, obtaining and verifying measurements, and documenting and communicating
questions.explanation: The scope is imaging, measurement, observation, documentation, and communication.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: An automated measurement appears on the screen. What is the sonographer's responsibility?
options: Accept all automated values without review
Obtain and verify the measurement — do not simply accept an automated value because it appears on the screen
Refer every value to a patient
questions.explanation: Image quality, tracing, and consistency must be checked before a measurement is accepted.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: Which set correctly lists recognized echo limitations?
options: Poor acoustic windows, arrhythmia, patient movement, and inability to tolerate positioning
questions.explanation: These are the technical and patient-related limitations the sonographer must recognize and report.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: Why must limitations be recognized and reported?
options: So the interpreting physician knows what can and cannot be concluded from the study
questions.explanation: Recognized and reported limitations let the physician judge the study's conclusions appropriately.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: Which statement about performing procedures is correct?
options: Anything in the profession's scope may be performed by anyone
An order alone authorizes any procedure
A procedure may fall within the profession but still require additional education, demonstrated competence, supervision, and organizational approval
questions.explanation: Profession-wide scope does not remove individual requirements of education, competence, supervision, and approval.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: What does "confidence alone never creates permission" mean?
options: Feeling ready does not establish education, competence, authorization, or policy approval
questions.explanation: Permission comes from demonstrated competence and authorization, not from self-assurance.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: A student has watched a procedure once. What does this establish?
options: Watching a procedure once does not automatically prepare the student to perform it
questions.explanation: Observation is not equivalent to training, demonstrated competence, or authorization.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: What is the difference between scope and boundaries?
options: Scope tells us what we contribute; boundaries tell us when another person or process is required
questions.explanation: Scope defines contribution; boundaries mark where another role or process must take over.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: What do professional boundaries represent?
options: A safe way to help — not a failure to help
questions.explanation: Boundaries keep care safe by ensuring the right person or process handles each need.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: Which statement about diagnosis and treatment is correct?
options: Sonographers may share results with family at will
Sonographers do not independently diagnose or prescribe treatment, and do not disclose diagnostic results outside the authorized process
questions.explanation: Diagnosis, prescribing, and result disclosure follow defined roles and authorized processes.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: What is the best redirect when a patient asks for a diagnostic conclusion?
options: "The interpreting physician reviews the complete study, and the results will be discussed through the usual care process."
questions.explanation: The redirect is honest about the role and points to the proper process.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: Why should a sonographer ask for help early when uncertain?
options: The earlier we ask, the more options the team has — waiting until the echo is over may make missing images or reassessment harder
questions.explanation: Early questions preserve options such as obtaining missing images or reassessing the patient.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: Which statement about speaking up is TRUE?
options: Only complete diagnoses should be raised
Speaking up is the physician's job
The sonographer does not need to independently solve the diagnostic uncertainty before speaking up
questions.explanation: Enough objective information to recognize the need for timely review is sufficient to raise a concern.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: What does asking for a second set of images review demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Requesting review of images is a professional judgement that protects the patient.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: During an echo-guided procedure, what is the sonographer's authority?
options: Holding the probe does not give the sonographer authority over the entire procedure — the responsible physician directs it
questions.explanation: The sonographer's role in procedures is defined and limited; the physician holds responsibility.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: Which statement BEST captures safe participation in an echo-guided procedure?
options: Improvisation before, assumptions during, and silence after
Role clarity before the procedure, objective communication during it, and complete documentation after
Documentation only if something goes wrong
questions.explanation: Clarity, objective communication, and complete documentation define safe participation.
tags: Scope of the Cardiac Sonographer and Professional Boundaries

questions.stem: What is interprofessional collaboration?
options: Working alone in a shared building
Working with other professionals toward a shared patient care goal — more than several people completing tasks in the same building
questions.explanation: Collaboration is goal-directed joint work, not mere co-location.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: Which statement about respect among the team is correct?
options: Respect includes how we treat colleagues during stressful moments, such as a code blue
questions.explanation: Stressful moments are precisely where respectful conduct matters most.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: Why should a sonographer not try to become every member of the healthcare team?
options: Safe care comes from knowing your role, recognizing when another expertise is needed, and ensuring information reaches the right person
questions.explanation: Role clarity — not role expansion — protects the patient.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: What is the nurse's particular value in recognizing patient change?
options: The nurse's ongoing assessment over time often detects changes between diagnostic encounters
questions.explanation: Continuous presence over time makes the nurse's observations of change especially valuable.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: What does the team depend on from the sonographer?
options: Observations that are clear, accurate, and timely
questions.explanation: Clear, accurate, timely observations are the sonographer's core team contribution.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: A colleague gives you critical feedback about your communication. What does accountability require?
questions.explanation: Accountability includes receiving feedback and changing practice where warranted.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: Feedback you receive is vague. What is the best response?
options: Ask for a specific example so the issue can be understood and addressed
questions.explanation: A specific example makes feedback actionable.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: Which statement about respect and safety is TRUE?
options: Safety concerns should be softened into hints
Respect does not mean silence when safety is at risk
questions.explanation: A safety concern must be stated clearly and escalated, respectfully but firmly.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: During a disagreement about priorities, what shared goal should be named?
options: The patient's safe assessment and care
questions.explanation: Naming the shared patient-safety goal reframes the disagreement productively.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: Which statement best captures effective interprofessional collaboration?
options: Each professional contributes their knowledge and authority, communicates clearly, and connects the patient to the next person with the right expertise
questions.explanation: Complementary roles, clear communication, and appropriate connection define collaboration.
tags: Interprofessional Collaboration

questions.stem: What is the FIRST step when an urgent observation is recognized?
options: Recognize the observation, change, or symptom for what it is
questions.explanation: Recognition begins the escalation process; the observation must be identified as significant.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: What is the second escalation step?
options: Assess immediate safety and patient stability within your role — look at the patient, not only the image
questions.explanation: Assessment of the patient's immediate safety determines the urgency of the response.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: Which pathway is appropriate for escalation?
options: The approved escalation pathway — such as the cardiologist, the patient's nurse, team lead, most responsible physician, or emergency response
questions.explanation: Escalation moves through designated, approved pathways.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: How should an urgent concern be communicated?
options: Clearly and without delay, stating what changed, what was observed, and why review is needed
Vaguely, such as "can someone come look at this when they have time?"
Only in writing at the end of the day
questions.explanation: Vague requests do not convey urgency; specific statements enable timely review.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: What must follow the escalation message?
options: Confirmation that the message was received and understood — and continuation to the next approved level if there is no response
questions.explanation: Without confirmation, the escalation may have failed; the pathway continues until someone responds.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: Why is leaving a voicemail inadequate for an urgent concern?
options: Leaving a voicemail is not confirmation that an urgent concern reached someone
questions.explanation: Urgent concerns require confirmation of receipt, which a voicemail cannot provide.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: What should be documented after an escalation?
options: Only that the study was completed
The observation, the person contacted, the timing, and the next step — without unsupported conclusions
Only your opinion of the cause
questions.explanation: Documentation of escalation captures facts — observation, contact, timing, next step.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: Which statement about urgent observations is TRUE?
options: An urgent observation is valuable once documented
An urgent observation matters only if the patient asks
An urgent observation has no value if it stays on our machine
An urgent observation belongs only to the sonographer
questions.explanation: Observations create value only when they reach someone who can act on them.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: What is required before raising a concern?
options: Enough objective information to recognize that the patient or study requires timely review — not a perfect diagnosis
questions.explanation: You don't need a perfect diagnosis before raising a concern.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: What is escalation, properly understood?
options: How the system prevents one missed message from becoming a patient safety failure — not punishment
questions.explanation: Escalation is a safety mechanism, not a disciplinary one.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: What does "stop treating the echo as routine when the patient is no longer routine" mean?
options: When the patient's condition changes, the examination's routine plan yields to assessment and escalation
questions.explanation: A changing patient demands a change in the examination's priorities and communication.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: The patient appears unstable. What takes priority?
options: The local emergency process — we do not move slowly through every box while the patient worsens
questions.explanation: Immediate emergency action takes precedence over sequential checklist completion.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: Jordan becomes more short of breath with a new large pericardial effusion, and the first cardiology contact does not answer. What is the correct action?
options: Stay with Jordan, obtain help, and continue through the approved escalation pathway
Wait for the final report before acting
Leave a voicemail and return to scanning
questions.explanation: Staying with the patient and continuing escalation protects the patient while awaiting response.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: Which sequence of escalation actions is complete?
options: Document → forget → assume → delay → deny → ignore
Guess → call → leave → hope → wait → blame
Recognize → assess immediate safety → follow the approved pathway → communicate objectively without delay → confirm receipt → document
questions.explanation: The full escalation sequence includes recognition, assessment, pathway, communication, confirmation, and documentation.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: Why must documentation after escalation avoid unsupported conclusions?
options: Documentation should show what happened, not simply defend the sonographer afterward
Conclusions are always prohibited by law
questions.explanation: Fact-centred documentation serves patients and review; self-serving conclusions do not.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: Which statement BEST captures the purpose of escalation in patient care?
options: When the patient's condition changes, communication becomes part of the treatment
questions.explanation: Timely communication is itself a component of treatment when conditions change.
tags: Urgent Findings and Escalation

questions.stem: What does SBAR stand for?
questions.explanation: SBAR structures an urgent message so the receiver understands immediately.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: What belongs in the Situation component?
options: What is happening now — identifying yourself, the patient, and the immediate concern
questions.explanation: The situation orients the receiver to who and what the message concerns right now.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: What belongs in the Background component?
options: Relevant context only — the information that matters for this decision right now, not the entire history
questions.explanation: Background is limited to what bears on the current decision.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: What belongs in the Assessment component?
options: The objective observations you contribute — symptom change, vital signs if available, and the concerning imaging observation
An independent diagnosis stated as certainty
A request to ignore the patient
questions.explanation: Assessment carries objective observations while staying within the sonographer's role.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Why should the Assessment avoid presenting an independent diagnosis as certainty?
options: The sonographer contributes observations; the interpreting physician integrates them into a diagnosis
questions.explanation: Staying within role keeps the message accurate and credible.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: What belongs in the Recommendation/request component?
options: A vague hope that someone checks
A summary of the entire admission
What action or review is needed
questions.explanation: A specific request tells the receiver exactly what to do.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Which closing phrase undermines an SBAR message?
options: "I need an urgent clinical review in the echo lab now."
"I just wanted to let you know" — it leaves the receiver to guess what you actually need
questions.explanation: A vague closing erases the request the message was built to deliver.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Which statement about the model SBAR message is correct?
options: The diagnosis is required in the Assessment
Background should include the entire history
"I observed a new large pericardial effusion" is an objective observation; "Jordan definitely has cardiac tamponade" would be an unsupported diagnosis
questions.explanation: A large effusion can have different haemodynamic effects, so the observation — not a diagnosis — is reported.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Which part of the model message "I need an urgent clinical review in the echo lab now" represents?
questions.explanation: The explicit statement of needed action is the R component.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Can SBAR be used for routine communication?
options: No — SBAR is only for emergencies
Yes — SBAR also works for a routine handoff, though wording and urgency change
Only written messages may use SBAR
questions.explanation: The structure adapts to routine handoffs with appropriate wording and urgency.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Which SBAR assessment statement is best?
options: "Jordan is becoming more short of breath, the blood pressure is now lower than on arrival, and I observed a new large pericardial effusion."
questions.explanation: The statement presents objective observations without converting them into a diagnosis.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Which element is missing from a message that states only "Jordan is becoming more short of breath"?
options: Background, Assessment, and the explicit Recommendation/request
questions.explanation: The symptom statement is the Situation only; a complete SBAR adds context, observations, and a clear request.
tags: SBAR and Structured Communication

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly matches the cardiac patient's diagnostic journey?
options: Referral and initial assessment → diagnostic testing and imaging → treatment planning or intervention → ongoing monitoring and follow-up
questions.explanation: The journey moves from referral through testing, planning, and follow-up.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: Why does the quality of the referral matter?
options: The quality of the referral affects how well the examination is prepared and focused
questions.explanation: A referral containing the real clinical question produces a more useful examination.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: Why should you always check whether a patient has had a previous echo?
options: The team looks for change over time, so previous studies provide the comparison that makes the current study meaningful
questions.explanation: Serial comparison — such as a previously mild effusion now large — is central to cardiac decision-making.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: Why do reproducible images and accurate measurements matter?
options: Because change over time is judged by comparing reproducible measurements across studies
questions.explanation: If measurements are not reproducible, apparent change may be measurement variation rather than disease.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: Which structures and functions does echocardiography evaluate?
options: Chamber size, ventricular function, valves, the pericardium, and haemodynamics
questions.explanation: These are the echo-evaluated structures and functions taught in the module.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: How does the interpreting physician use the echocardiogram?
options: By combining it with history, physical examination, ECG, laboratory results, and other investigations to support diagnosis and treatment planning
By reading the images in isolation
By relying on the sonographer's diagnosis
questions.explanation: Echo findings gain meaning within the complete clinical picture.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: How does echocardiography support ongoing care?
options: Only by providing a single baseline
By monitoring disease progression through serial studies and assessing response to treatment — improved, stable, or worsened
Only by confirming a single diagnosis
questions.explanation: Serial studies track progression and treatment response over time.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: Which set correctly lists echocardiography's limitations?
options: Coronary anatomy, fine rhythm detail, tissue characterization, and exercise response may require other tests
questions.explanation: Knowing what echo cannot answer directs appropriate additional testing.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: What does "guides clinical decision making" mean about the echocardiogram?
options: It informs decisions — the image does not make the decision
questions.explanation: Echo evidence informs — but does not independently determine — clinical decisions.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: Which test matches the question "What is the rhythm over a longer period?"
questions.explanation: Ambulatory monitoring records rhythm over an extended period, catching intermittent problems.
tags: Echo Within Cardiac Patient Management and Other Tests

questions.stem: Where does most workplace conflict begin?
options: With a problem in the work, not necessarily a problem with the people
questions.explanation: Framing conflict as a work problem directs attention to fixable causes.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: How should miscommunication as a conflict cause be addressed?
options: By checking understanding and confirming messages — unclear, incomplete, or unconfirmed information causes conflict
questions.explanation: Confirming messages prevents the misunderstandings that fuel conflict.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: Which is an example of unclear role expectations causing conflict?
options: Disagreement over who obtains vital signs, arranges transport, prepares contrast, contacts the physician, or monitors the patient after the echo
A disagreement about image quality standards
questions.explanation: These role questions are common sources of departmental conflict.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: A competing-priorities conflict involves which situation?
options: The emergency department wants an urgent study while an unstable inpatient is being scanned and a full outpatient schedule is waiting
questions.explanation: Simultaneous competing demands are a classic cause of workplace conflict.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: Two colleagues have different communication styles. What is the correct understanding?
options: Different styles do not automatically mean that either person is unprofessional
questions.explanation: Style differences alone do not indicate unprofessional conduct.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: Staffing shortages and equipment unavailability cause conflict in what way?
options: People may begin blaming one another for a problem created by the system
questions.explanation: System-created resource problems are often misattributed to individuals.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: What is the first resolution step when conflict arises?
options: Listen actively first — for example, "What I'm hearing is that you're worried about the delay. Is that correct?"
questions.explanation: Active listening confirms the real concern before solutions are discussed.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: Where should a difficult conversation with a colleague take place?
options: Away from patients and other staff
questions.explanation: Privacy protects patients, colleagues, and the conversation itself.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: What is the purpose of asking, "Can you explain what you're expecting from me?"
options: To clarify misunderstandings early before they escalate
questions.explanation: Early clarification of expectations resolves many conflicts before they grow.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: What does returning to the shared goal sound like?
options: "We both want Jordan assessed safely. Let us decide what needs to happen first."
questions.explanation: Naming the shared goal reframes the discussion around the patient.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: What does working toward a clear solution involve?
options: Explaining what you can do, identifying what you need, and confirming the next action
Making the other person decide everything
questions.explanation: Concrete contributions, needs, and next actions produce resolution.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: When should a conflict be escalated?
options: At the first sign of disagreement
When the patient remains at risk, the concern is outside your authority, the behaviour is serious, or the problem continues despite reasonable attempts
questions.explanation: These four circumstances justify escalation beyond the immediate conversation.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: A nurse says, "Echo keeps delaying my patient." What is the best response?
options: "I understand that you are concerned about the delay. I'm currently scanning an unstable patient. Your patient is next, but if their condition has changed, tell me now so we can reassess their priority together."
questions.explanation: The response acknowledges the concern, explains the situation, and invites reassessment if the condition has changed.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: Which statement best separates the issue from the person?
options: "You are unreliable," rather than describing the event
"The urgent message was not confirmed," rather than "You are unreliable."
questions.explanation: Describing the process problem addresses the issue without attacking identity.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: In the SBI feedback model, what belongs in the Behaviour component?
options: Your interpretation of the person's character
Only what you observed — such as "the urgent message was sent, but the receipt was not confirmed"
questions.explanation: Behaviour is limited to observable facts, which keeps feedback specific and fair.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: Which statement BEST captures the professional approach to conflict?
options: Conflict resolution does not require everyone to agree — it requires respectful communication, a clear next step, and escalation when the concern remains unresolved
questions.explanation: Respectful communication plus a clear next step plus escalation when needed defines professional conflict resolution.
tags: Workplace Conflict: Causes and Resolution

questions.stem: Jordan becomes more short of breath and the blood pressure drops during the echo. What does this moment illustrate?
options: The image is only the beginning — when the patient's condition changes, communication becomes part of the treatment
The study should be finished silently
Only the physician needs to notice
The report can wait until morning
questions.explanation: A changing patient transforms communication into an urgent component of care.
tags: Jordan's Turning Point, Practice Questions and Capstone

questions.stem: A patient asks during the examination, "Did you find anything serious?" What is the most appropriate response?
options: Show the images and let the patient interpret them
Explain the review process and connect the patient with the appropriate clinician — without giving your own interpretation or false reassurance
Say "I can't tell you anything" and turn away
questions.explanation: Explaining the review process and connecting the patient to the clinician answers honestly within role.
tags: Jordan's Turning Point, Practice Questions and Capstone

questions.stem: A colleague dismisses a safety concern you raise. What is the correct response?
options: Drop the concern to keep the peace
Restate it clearly and continue through the approved escalation pathway
Wait for the patient to deteriorate
questions.explanation: Respectful persistence through the approved pathway ensures the concern is heard.
tags: Jordan's Turning Point, Practice Questions and Capstone

questions.stem: What was the sonographer's job in Jordan's case?
options: Not to solve everything alone — to acquire the information, recognize the change, protect the patient, and bring the appropriate people into the decision
To wait for instructions without acting
questions.explanation: Acquisition, recognition, protection, and connection — not solo resolution — define the sonographer's role.
tags: Jordan's Turning Point, Practice Questions and Capstone

questions.stem: Which statement BEST captures what makes a safe professional?
options: A strong sonographer produces good images; a safe professional also knows when to communicate, when to ask for help, and how to remain part of a team until the concern has an appropriate next step
questions.explanation: Image quality plus communication, help-seeking, and team participation define safe practice.
tags: Jordan's Turning Point, Practice Questions and Capstone

questions.stem: Which combination BEST represents the sonographer within the healthcare team as presented in this module?
options: Work alone, communicate only at shift change, ignore barriers, diagnose independently, avoid escalation, and let conflict resolve itself
Follow protocols rigidly, share everything with everyone, escalate without confirmation, and rank team roles

Practise with professionalism and accountability, communicate clearly and confirm the loop, adapt to barriers with empathy, share relevant and objective information through approved channels, know your scope and boundaries, escalate urgent observations without delay, use SBAR, and resolve conflict respectfully around the shared patient goal
Focus exclusively on image quality and leave communication to physicians
questions.explanation: Each element reflects a core expectation of the module — teamwork built on clear communication, defined role, timely escalation, and respectful collaboration.
tags: Jordan's Turning Point, Practice Questions and Capstone
